text: {"question":"In the PEDE model, which combination of observational data (CC, SNIa, BAO, CMB) produces the tightest reconstruction of the deceleration parameter q(z), and how does adding an MB prior to a different cosmological model influence the degeneracy between the Hubble constant and dark‑energy parameters?","reference_answer":"The tightest q(z) reconstruction in the PEDE model is obtained when all four data sets—CC, SNIa, BAO, and CMB—are combined. Introducing an MB prior in other models (e.g., Varying me or WZDR) further explores the H₀–parameter degeneracy, generally reducing the preference for dynamical dark‑energy signatures by shifting the w₀–wₐ constraints."}
